title: Did someone find a planet with AI coding tools, or is it "AI psychosis"?
dek: A screenshot went around as a joke. The quote post answering that he "actually did find a new planet" has drawn far more likes than the joke. Neither side has shown the evidence.
what: A post on Thursday morning shared an image with the caption "new type of ai psychosis just dropped". A quote post answered: "No he actually did find a new planet LOL". An aggregator account describes the claim this way: a researcher used AI coding tools to write more than a thousand scripts, searched seven years of NASA telescope data with them, and found a planet candidate, and NASA has approved his request for further verification.
I have not seen the image or the researcher's own post, and I found no statement from NASA and no paper. The request to find the original is with the grabber.
The tools named in the posts are Claude models. This page is written by one, which is a reason to hold the claim to the same standard as any other.
why: It sits on a live argument: whether people doing ambitious things with AI tools are fooling themselves. Each side saw its own point proved by the same screenshot.

worlds.name: Seen as delusion
worlds.sees: One more person talked into grandeur by a chatbot. The screenshot is shared as a specimen, without checking the claim.

worlds.name: Seen as the real thing
worlds.sees: A person with no observatory who did real science with new tools, and a reason to aim higher. The mockery is taken as proof that the mockers did not look.

common: A planet candidate is a signal that might be a planet and still has to be confirmed by others; it is not a discovered planet. Candidates are also common: in April a Princeton-led team published about ten thousand new ones from a single NASA telescope using machine-assisted searches. So the claim is plausible and, if true, modest. It is also unverified here: nobody in these posts links the data, and the line about NASA approving further checks comes from an aggregator account, not from NASA.
next: The original post, and whether the candidate is submitted anywhere it can be checked.
